action_items.text: C will try to find out if it's possible to make a rechargeable remote and what it would cost to implement.
C will try to gather financial information about the costs and materials for the remote.
B will draw up some designs of possible remote controls based on the essentials discussed.
B will post the designs on the product share for review.
C will look into the feasibility of including an L_C_D_ screen and speech recognition, determining costs and space requirements.
The group will collectively think of a name for the remote control.
A will share the meeting minutes on the web shortly.

decisions.text: The power button should be placed centrally and not at the top or somewhere else where it can be pressed accidentally.
The power button should be on top because it is the first thing you do when turning on the remote.
The mute button should be placed somewhere at the bottom, not near the volume or channel buttons.
Channel up and down buttons should be placed on top, making them easily accessible.
The remote should include a feature to locate the remote (beep and/or flash) when it is lost.
They will consider a combination of beep and flashing light for locating the remote rather than just a flash.
The remote should have a design that is easy to use, with important buttons (power, channel, volume) placed prominently.
They will not focus on features like an L_C_D_ screen and speech recognition for the age group under 40, due to potential cost and usability concerns.
They will explore the feasibility of including an L_C_D_ screen based on cost and space requirements, despite it being a desired feature.
They will keep the remote's design simple and focused on ease of use, with a potential luxury version including an L_C_D_ screen.
They will decide on a name for the remote control.
